    {ΩB : Type*} [MeasurableSpace ΩB]
    (B : ℝ≥0 → ΩB → ℝ) (PB : Measure ΩB) [IsProbabilityMeasure PB]
    (hB : IsBrownianReal B PB) (x : ℝ) :
    Shao.standardNormalTail x ≤ PB.real {omegaB | ∃ t : BridgeTime,
        x ≤ |B ⟨(t : ℝ), t.property.1⟩ omegaB|} := by

theorem brownian_weak_absolute_crossing_lower
    {ΩB : Type*} [MeasurableSpace ΩB]
    (B : ℝ≥0 → ΩB → ℝ) (PB : Measure ΩB) [IsProbabilityMeasure PB]
    (hB : IsBrownianReal B PB) (x : ℝ) :
    Shao.standardNormalTail x ≤ PB.real {omegaB | ∃ t : BridgeTime,
        x ≤ |B ⟨(t : ℝ), t.property.1⟩ omegaB|} := by
  have hEndpoint : PB.real {omegaB | x < B 1 omegaB} = Shao.standardNormalTail x := by
    exact (hB.toIsPreBrownianReal.hasLaw_eval 1).measureReal_eq measurableSet_Ioi
  rw [← hEndpoint]
  apply ENNReal.toReal_mono (measure_ne_top _ _)
  apply measure_mono
  intro omegaB homega
  refine ⟨(1 : BridgeTime), ?_⟩
  change x ≤ |B 1 omegaB|
  exact homega.le.trans (le_abs_self _)

ownerCoverage.proofReview: The endpoint law is HasLaw (B 1) (gaussianReal 0 1) PB, obtained from the same native hB and the same PB. HasLaw.measureReal_eq is applied to the measurable Ioi predicate x<z. Its right side is definitionally Shao.standardNormalTail x. Rewriting by that equality leaves real-measure monotonicity. PB is a probability measure, hence finite, so measure_ne_top applies to the entire target set without a measurability premise; ENNReal.toReal_mono therefore has its required finite right-hand argument. Pointwise inclusion sends omegaB with x<B 1 omegaB to the literal t=1 in BridgeTime. The NNReal made from that time is definitionally 1. The final inequality is x<=B 1 omegaB<=abs(B 1 omegaB). Strict-to-weak conversion uses homega.le, with no sign restriction on x and no exceptional-set or continuity replacement.

proofSummary: Let E_x={omegaB | x<B 1 omegaB} and A_x={omegaB | exists t in [0,1], x<=abs(B_t omegaB)}, with the physical NNReal evaluation used in the source. Native Brownian finite-dimensional laws give PB.real E_x=Psi(x). Every omegaB in E_x belongs to A_x by choosing t=1 and using x<B_1<=abs(B_1). Finite-measure monotonicity yields Psi(x)<=PB.real A_x. Since Psi(x)>0 for every finite real x, PB.real A_x>0. If x<=1, antitonicity gives Psi(1)<=Psi(x)<=PB.real A_x.
